scope: Offline comparison of hash-pinned 20/10/5 um fixed-event fields at a shared physical X section, section-phase sweeps, and a frozen 5 um field sampled onto coarse coordinates. No NIST raw payload, parameter tuning, or 12.5 ns run.

physicalSectionPhaseSweep.mesh20_x110_um: no-melt; width and depth remain null

frozenFineFieldOnCoarseCoordinates.interpolation: trilinear nodal temperature interpolation with bounds_error=true

interpretation: At the common X=100 um section, width increases from 43.2918 to 50.7151 um but is not converged. All top boundaries remain molten and substrate liquidus cells are zero, so substrate depth=0 is not a melt-pool depth comparison. Cell-supported widths (40/40/50 um) hide part of the change. Moving X changes the physical section, so the phase sweep is not a pure quantization error. Sampling the same fine temperature field onto coarse coordinates shows strong support/representation sensitivity at 20 um and a larger coarse-field term for 10 um under this interpolation choice. Trilinear temperature sampling is not conservative enthalpy transfer, and the 5 um run had 1673 source-limited retries versus zero for the coarser runs; therefore this decomposition is diagnostic, not pure mesh error or physical causality.
nextStep: On the same frozen fields, evaluate a conservative enthalpy-volume projection before considering finer transient steps; preserve no-melt nulls and the current inconclusive convergence and unvalidated model labels.
